newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm, but checked by dlr puts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm, but checked by dlr puts.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed firmer for the third session in a row on Tuesday due to falling long bond yields, although traders noted several players decided to exercise dollar puts which halted the peso's advance.
"They exercised (puts) today, but the stage was set for the peso to firm to 7.92 per dollar," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed trade 0.6 of a centavo firmer at 7.9250/7.9290 and 7.9220/7.9250 per dollar, respectively.
Banco de Mexico auctions at least $300 million in puts each month, which may be exercised on any business day the following month, subject to conditions.

Dealers said the peso had gained much of its strength earlier in the session as falling U.S. long bond yields triggered a flow of dollars into the Mexican market, to take advantage of expected increases in domestic primary rates.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 20/32 to yield 6.74 percent shortly after the foreign exchange market had closed in Mexico.
In a Reuters survey, money market dealers predicted bellwether 28-day Cetes rates would increase by an average of 18 basis points at Tuesday night's primary auction.
Nonetheless, they predicted rates on longer term issues could fall.
"Falling rates could hit the peso tomorrow," another trader said.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 2.1 centavos firmer at 7.9210/7.9240 per dollar.
